summary: Six rules whose second-order effect reverses their first-order intent, all measured against the commit record. The prompt's own candidate ('chaos-plant every guard' -> slower iteration -> fewer experiments) is REFUTED on its stated mechanism and reversed on a different one. The strongest finding is that judging is generative: from 7a9a7d9 (2026-08-23) onward the L0 claim pool grew faster than judgement closed it, so gate L0-B moved AWAY from green with every wave, and the only exit was an owner ruling that KILLED 128 unexamined claims -- a completeness gate satisfied by discarding evidence. Net standing-rule word delta of all proposed changes: -13.

findings.claim: GAUNTLET.md §0 ('a VOID verdict returns its finding to the pool UNJUDGED') combined with §3.5 ('loop until two consecutive rounds surface nothing new') makes judging GENERATIVE, so past a measured crossover on 2026-08-23 every judging wave moved gate L0-B 'NOTHING UNJUDGED' further from green -- the completeness rule's second-order effect is that completeness becomes unreachable by work.

findings.proposed_change: Replace docs/GAUNTLET.md:193 '**LOOP UNTIL DRY.** Keep spawning finders until **two consecutive rounds surface nothing new**. Dedup against everything *seen*, not everything *confirmed* — otherwise critic-rejected findings reappear each round and the loop never converges.' with '**LOOP WHILE THE POOL SHRINKS.** Spawn finders while unjudged is falling. A round that pools more claims than it judges is generative, not convergent — stop and take a ruling. Dedup against everything *seen*, not everything *confirmed*.' Incident it would have prevented: waves at 2f8d88d/ab93692/7bc726b/0d8aa6d each raised unjudged; the rule would have fired at 2f8d88d and stopped four waves and one wall earlier. Second-order consequence, stated honestly: a genuinely productive burst that briefly out-pools its judging gets stopped early, and the operator must take a ruling to continue -- more rulings, fewer autonomous rounds. Rollback: git revert the one-line edit; §3.5's old text is in the commit.

findings.claim: The prompt's candidate is REFUTED on its stated mechanism -- guards did NOT slow iteration -- but the rule reverses on a different mechanism: 'chaos-plant every guard' is target-agnostic, so it faithfully hardened whatever the session was touching, and once the session was touching PROCESS, every one of the 7 new guards protected the review machinery and none protected the game. Test LOC overtook src LOC for the first time on 2026-08-23 while src LOC did not move by a single byte.

findings.rule_targeted: CLAUDE.md:37 'Chaos-test every guard: plant the failure, watch red, fix, watch green.'
findings.proposed_change: Do NOT weaken CLAUDE.md:37 -- it is in §1's proven set and D2 proves the process scripts needed guards. The change is a DELETION in the session doc: strike the now-falsified parenthetical from docs/sessions/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_KICKOFF.md §3, row 'Second-Order Thinking' -- '(Candidate: "chaos-plant every guard" -> more guards -> slower iteration -> fewer experiments run.)' -- because the suite runs in 14.69s, guards postdate the src stall by 23 days, and src/tests commits moved in lockstep for four weeks. Leaving a measured-false causal chain in a kickoff sends the next lens hunting a mechanism that does not exist. Incident: this lens spent its first three measurements refuting it. Second-order consequence: the kickoff loses a worked example of how to phrase a lens question. Rollback: restore the parenthetical from 2df2f87. (Session doc, not a standing rule, so word_delta against standing rules is 0.)

findings.claim: CLAUDE.md:48 'RESUME_HERE.md — refreshed in the SAME commit as the change it describes' has the second-order effect of making the handoff append-only: 'refreshed' permits adding, so nothing is ever removed. The doc grew 78% in four days during which src/ received zero commits, and it now ships a block explicitly headed 'SUPERSEDED ... ITS STATE NUMBERS ARE STALE' -- the rule that guarantees freshness produced a document that must warn the reader which half of it has rotted.

findings.rule_targeted: CLAUDE.md:48 'RESUME_HERE.md (repo root) — refreshed in the SAME commit as the change it describes.'
findings.proposed_change: Change CLAUDE.md:48 to '- `RESUME_HERE.md` (repo root) — **rewritten, not appended to**, in the SAME commit as the change it describes.' One word swap forbids the append that produced the 599-line archive; superseded blocks go to docs/sessions/-SESSION-LOG.md, which already exists for exactly that. Incident it would have prevented: the SESSION 26 block surviving into 2df2f87 under a 'STATE NUMBERS ARE STALE' banner, in the one document a fresh session is told to read first. Second-order consequence: a rewrite can drop a correction the appender would have kept (C1/C2/C3 are the live example), so the rewrite must move them rather than delete them -- moving is a manual step and manual steps get skipped. Rollback: restore the word 'refreshed'.

findings.claim: CLAUDE.md:44 'Pre-commit runs typecheck -> tests. Commit = green' defines 'green' entirely over code. Its second-order effect, now that the project's output has been prose for 27 days, is that the gate reports GREEN on commits that ship falsehoods: 22% of commits since 2026-08-13 hit .githooks/pre-commit's docs-only fast-path and ran no check at all, and no check anywhere reads a claim in a markdown file.

if [ -n "$STAGED" ] && [ -z "$NON_DOC" ]; then

findings.rule_targeted: CLAUDE.md:44 'Pre-commit runs typecheck → tests (see `.githooks/pre-commit`). Commit = green.'
findings.proposed_change: Edit .githooks/pre-commit only (zero standing-rule words): narrow the fast-path's NON_DOC filter so `docs/research/*.md` and `docs/GAUNTLET.md` do NOT qualify as skippable -- those are the files gateL0.py and tests/gauntletL0Gate.test.ts actually parse, so an edit to them can break a real check. Incident it would have prevented: any markdown-only edit to REBUILD_READINESS.md during L0 committed without the gate test running; the file is gateL0.py's --ledger input and 47 August commits touched docs/. Second-order consequence: ledger edits get 20s slower, which during a rewrite wave of 14 slices is real friction and will tempt --no-verify. Rollback: one-line revert of the grep pattern.

findings.claim: This review's own gate ARCH-E ('total net change to standing-rule WORD count is <= 0') reverses on contact: the cheapest words to delete are rationale, not imperatives, and this repo's own record shows rationale is the only thing that makes a wrong rule auditable. D6 exists solely because §3.8 wrote down BOTH of its reasons -- 62 words of rationale that a word-budget optimiser deletes first, taking the audit trail with it.
findings.evidence:
$ grep -n 'ARCH-E' docs/sessions/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_KICKOFF.md
187:- **ARCH-E** Total net change to standing-rule word count is **≤ 0**. The rules may be
$ (word count of §3.8's block in docs/GAUNTLET.md)
§3.8 block words: 301
reason-1 rationale words: 62
D6, verbatim from the kickoff: 'The one-workflow rule has two reasons. The second ... is airtight and sufficient on its own. The first (concurrency is what causes the wall) is weaker: this session ran strictly serially and still hit wall #11.' That defect is only discoverable because the 62 words were written down. ARCH-E scores those 62 words as pure cost. Note also that §1 and §6 fence off the seven proven rules, so the entire word budget must be paid out of unproven prose -- which is where rationale lives.
findings.proposed_change: Change ARCH-E to '**ARCH-E** Total net change to standing-rule COUNT is **≤ 0**. The rules may be fewer or sharper; rationale is free. *(This is the anti-bloat gate. It is deliberately harsh.)*' Bloat is measured in rules a reader must hold, not in characters. Incident it would have prevented: none yet -- ARCH-E is one commit old (2df2f87) -- but its first application is this review, and under a word budget the highest-value deletion available to any lens is a rationale block, which is how D6 became knowable. Second-order consequence: a rule-count budget lets prose grow unboundedly around a fixed rule set, and long rules get skimmed; the mitigation is that ARCH-C still forces at least one deletion. Rollback: restore 'word count' and the old second sentence.

findings.claim: CLAUDE.md:36 ('do not advance until the current stage's gate is 100% green') plus GAUNTLET.md R2 ('L0 runs before any other lane') has the second-order effect that ONE unclosable document-survey gate freezes all twelve lanes -- including L1, whose gate reads questdata.xml and never reads the ledger. Eleven days, 51 commits, zero commits to src/.

findings.proposed_change: DELETE R2 as written and replace with the scoped form: '**R2 — L0 gates only the lanes that READ the ledger.** L1's inputs are `questdata.xml`, not `REBUILD_READINESS.md`, so it may run in parallel. > **Veto:** hold L1 until L0 closes.' Second-order consequence, stated honestly: L1 would build a campaign runtime against a scorecard that L0 may still re-score, so if L0 later overturns a quests-story claim, L1 rework is possible -- bounded, because L1's gate is byte-exactness against the XML, which L0 cannot change. Rollback: restore R2's original 50 words from 2df2f87; §2's ordering rule at :139 is untouched either way.
